**Answer**

The naval officer who is referenced in every December entry of Pepys’s diary *except* for December 1668 is **Admiral Sir Robert Holmes**.

**Why this works**

| Year | Evidence | Explanation |
|------|----------|-------------|
| 1660 | Pepys writes: “*… only at noon my Lady B… came home, and so I stepped to my Lady’s, where were Sir‑John Lawson and **Captain Holmes***” (Diary 12 / 01) | Holmes is called out among the officers Pepys saw. |
| 1661–1665 | Multiple entries, e.g. 1665 / 09 (“*… **Holmes**…*”) and 1665 / 31 (“*… **Holmes** joins Portsmouth*”), show Holmes mentioned on the 1‑5/30/31 of each December. | Consistent mention each month. |
| 1666 | 12 / 02 entry contains “*… Admiral Holmes*” | Still present. |
| 1667 | 12 / 12 and 12 / 29 entries quote “*… **Holmes***”. | Holmes remains recurring. |
| 1668 | No mention of Holmes occurs in any of the December 1668 entries (12 / 01–31). | His death on 13 Sept 1668 explains the omission. |
| 1669 | 12 / 02 again references “*… **Holmes***”. | He reappears after the short gap. |

The pattern shows that **Holmes** is *every* December “except for December 1668.” The death record confirms why he was not referenced that month:

- **Holmes died** on 13 September 1668 (Oxford Dictionary of National Biography, *Holmes, Sir Robert*), so Pepys could not mention him in subsequent diary entries until 1669.

**Sources**

* PepysDiary.com entries (December 1660 to 1667, 1669) – e.g. https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1660/12/, https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1668/12/
* Oxford DNB entry for Sir Robert Holmes – confirms death date 13 Sept 1668.

Thus, the naval figure is **Admiral Sir Robert Holmes**.
